project.name: SDLC Artifact Factory
project.author: Shafi Babar
project.description: A Claude Code plugin that takes a problem statement and drives a product through its full SDLC lifecycle — Strategy → Ideate → Design → Implement → Data → Quality → Deploy → Customer Validation — producing real, reviewable, methodology-compliant artifacts at every phase.

working_agreements.operator: Shafi Babar. Product Manager. Solo operator (Han Solo). Not a programmer. Provides problem statements, reviews artifacts, approves each chunk before proceeding.
working_agreements.claude_role: Principal engineer. Does all implementation — skills, agents, commands, hooks, tools, code generation. Shafi approves; Claude builds.
working_agreements.session_startup: Read sdlc-context.json first. Restore context from this file, not from conversation history.
working_agreements.chunk_gate: After Chunk 4: each subsequent chunk is planned, discussed, and explicitly approved by Shafi before execution. No chunk starts without a go.
working_agreements.build_discipline: One chunk at a time. One commit per chunk. Nothing in a later chunk is started while an earlier chunk is incomplete.
working_agreements.budget_posture: Frugal. Open-source preferred. No paid APIs, no expensive tooling. Process and methodology are the investment, not tooling.
working_agreements.timeline: Iterative. No deadlines. Quality over speed.

non_negotiables: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) — Ubiquitous Language, Bounded Contexts, Domain Events, Aggregates
Event Storming — applied at Design phase for every domain and subdomain
Test-Driven Development (TDD) — tests written before implementation code, always
Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) — Gherkin feature files for all acceptance criteria
SOLID — applied across all generated code artifacts
methodology.enforcement: Absence of an applicable methodology in any artifact is a defect, not a warning. Phase gate hooks enforce compliance before advancing.

tech_stack._note: These are the default target-stack decisions. Parameterized per product at /sdlc-start time. Saved to sdlc-config.json per product.

confirmed.api_framework: net/http + chi — idiomatic, lightweight, no magic, code-reviewable. Chosen over Gin/Echo/Fiber for compliance-grade transparency.
confirmed.primary_database: PostgreSQL + pgx — ACID, audit log, config store, outbox table. Default for all services.
confirmed.search_and_alerts: Elasticsearch — document indexing, full-text search, alert storage.
confirmed.message_broker: Redpanda — Kafka-API compatible, no JVM, frugal, familiar Kafka tooling.
confirmed.graph_database: Apache AGE (default, PostgreSQL extension, zero extra infra). Neo4j Community as selectable alternative when graph is primary product surface.
confirmed.ci_cd: GitHub Actions — native to GitHub repos, free tier, zero hosting overhead.
confirmed.iac: OpenTofu (infrastructure provisioning, open-source Terraform fork) + Helm (application deployment onto Kubernetes).
confirmed.service_mesh: Linkerd — Rust data plane, automatic mTLS, lowest resource overhead, CNCF graduated.
confirmed.container_orchestration: Kubernetes. EKS/AKS/GKE via OpenTofu for customer cloud. k3s for managed private tenants. kind for local development. Single Helm chart per service, environment differences in values.yaml.
confirmed.observability: OpenTelemetry (Go SDK) + Prometheus (metrics) + Elasticsearch + Fluent Bit (logs) + Tempo (traces) + Grafana (single pane). Kibana optional for deep log analysis.
confirmed.optional_database: MongoDB — variable-schema bounded contexts (entity extraction output, crawl metadata). Exposed as config option at /sdlc-start. Not default.

tech_stack.sdlc_start_questionnaire: Interactive questionnaire at /sdlc-start saves answers to sdlc-config.json per product. Allows per-product overrides of defaults above.

first_product.name: Data Estate Mapping and Compliance Intelligence
first_product.core_value: Maps an organisation's data estate across storage systems, extracts entities, builds a relationship graph, and provides compliance intelligence — with zero data ever leaving customer infrastructure.
first_product.architecture_style: Event-driven microservices with physical tenant isolation
first_product.pipeline: Worker nodes at customer storage → Message Queue → File Processing → Entity Extraction → Graph Update → Compliance Rule Engine → Alert + Audit

plugin_architecture.description: Commands drive phases. Phases activate agents. Agents draw on skills for expertise and scripts (via Bash) for atomic actions. Hooks enforce governance automatically, calling scripts or consulting skills directly. Artifacts are outputs of the workflow, not the inputs.
plugin_architecture.component_hierarchy: Command → Agent → Skill | Agent → Script (via Bash) | Hook → Script or → Agent/Skill

axioms.Skills: Expertise — domain knowledge, standards, patterns. No reasoning.
axioms.Agents: Reasoning — decisions, analysis, design, code generation. Use skills for knowledge.
axioms.Commands: Workflows — user-facing phase drivers and cross-cutting operations.
axioms.Hooks: Governance — event-driven, lightweight, fast, idempotent. No business logic.
axioms.Scripts: Atomic actions — deterministic, stateless, single-purpose. Not a Claude Code discovery mechanism; 'Tools' means MCP-exposed tools specifically.

decisions.decision: Architecture pattern is workflow-first, not artifact-first
decisions.rationale: Commands drive phases. Agents activate within phases. Artifacts are outputs of the workflow. The previous build was artifact-first — a knowledge library, not a factory.

decisions.decision: Skills organized by knowledge domain, not SDLC phase
decisions.rationale: DDD, TDD, BDD apply across multiple phases. Phase-locked skills cause duplication or get skipped when the phase doesn't match. Domain organization makes skills reusable across phases.
alternatives_rejected: Phase-locked skills (strategy/, ideate/, design/, implement/ etc.) — used in old build, caused duplication

Renaming CLAUDE.md's required 'name' field to 'artifact' — would ripple into every governance rule

decisions.decision: Behavioral Directives in agents are an accepted pattern: a compressed index of imperative bullets, each citing the owning skill. Decision criteria/tables in skills are knowledge, not reasoning.
decisions.rationale: Codifies two boundary clarifications to the component anti-pattern rules. Directives whose substance is absent from the cited skill remain defects — the substance moves into the skill.
alternatives_rejected: Strict reading — stripping all directive content from agents into skills; loses the at-a-glance engineering contract without reducing duplication

decisions.decision: Content improvement campaign before Chunk 15: full per-file pass over all skills, agents, and repo metadata, delivered as five batch PRs.
decisions.rationale: A stronger model became available; three parallel audits found generational drift in agents, frontmatter schism, stale metadata, dead references, and terminology drift. Fixing before building Chunk 15 prevents propagating the drift into new components.
alternatives_rejected: Targeted fixes only — audit sampled ~20% of skills, so unsampled files would get no fresh scrutiny
Single campaign PR — a ~120-file diff is not PM-reviewable in one sitting

decisions.decision: Chunk 19 rebuilt commands/hooks conceptual spec (COMMAND.md/HOOK.md, invented lifecycle events, 'Tools' component) into real, verified Claude Code mechanics: commands/*.md slash commands, hooks/hooks.json, scripts/*.sh. Verified by loading this repo as a session plugin (`claude --plugin-dir`) and inspecting `claude plugin details` output plus one live command invocation, not just by reading the files for coherence.
decisions.rationale: The original commands/hooks/tools design (Chunks 1-3) predated any real Claude Code mechanics research and used fictional structure. Real testing caught concrete errors (invalid plugin.json fields, a YAML-breaking argument-hint) that static review would have missed.
alternatives_rejected: Continue conceptual spec documents — the plugin would remain unrunnable indefinitely

decisions.decision: Agents restructured from agents/<role>/AGENT.md (nested) to agents/<role>.md (flat) — folded into Chunk 19's PR. Confirmed empirically: a nested AGENT.md is not discovered by Claude Code's real agent-discovery mechanism; a flat <name>.md is.
decisions.rationale: Discovered while live-testing Chunk 19's commands via `claude plugin details` — Agents (0) despite 13 real agent files existing. Isolated the root cause with a controlled test copy before changing anything. Mechanical fix (file relocation only, no content change), low risk, same root-cause class as the commands/hooks fix already underway.
alternatives_rejected: Defer to a separate PR — rejected only for this specific fix since it was small, mechanical, and directly related; the same testing methodology surfaced a second, much larger issue (see open_questions) which WAS deferred

decisions.decision: Chunk 20's 9 originally-planned hooks consolidated to 7 real hooks.json entries: pre-phase-advance, pre-code-generation, and pre-implement collapsed into one pre-phase-advance hook (PreToolUse/Agent, gates any agent invocation on its phase's prerequisite artifacts) once bound to a real event — they were the identical check under three names. methodology-compliance-check implemented as an agent-type handler (not a script) since judging methodology compliance is inherently interpretive; the other 6 are command-type handlers backed by real scripts/*.sh.
decisions.rationale: Real Claude Code PreToolUse fires per tool call (e.g. every Agent dispatch), not per abstract 'phase' or 'code generation' event — there is no way to bind 3 separately-named hooks to 3 different real triggers when they'd all fire on the same event and check the same thing. Confirmed the tool name for subagent dispatch is 'Agent' with tool_input.subagent_type identifying which agent, by triggering a real dispatch and inspecting the hook's stdin JSON.
alternatives_rejected: Keep 9 separate hooks.json entries that run identical logic 3x on every Agent call — wasteful and dishonest about what they actually do

Make methodology-compliance-check a command-type script — rejected, methodology judgment is not reliably reducible to regex/deterministic checks (see the terminology-drift-detector script's own documented limitation on this)

decisions.decision: All 6 hook-backing scripts hardened after live testing surfaced 3 real bugs: naming-convention-enforcer's extraction regex silently let invalid names through instead of catching them (restrictive character class used for extraction, not just validation); post-artifact-created resolved the manifest path from cwd instead of the written file's own path, missing writes outside cwd; none of the 6 scripts protected their outermost JSON parse, so malformed stdin crashed with a Python traceback instead of failing open.
decisions.rationale: Each bug was found by actually invoking the hook with a real or synthetic trigger and checking the outcome, not by reading the script. The naming-convention bug in particular would have silently shipped a non-functional governance check — a live end-to-end test (create a badly-named file, confirm it's rejected) caught what a code read did not.
alternatives_rejected: Ship without live-testing each script individually — rejected per the standing practice this session established in Chunk 19 (D012)

decisions.decision: All 136 skills restructured from skills/<domain>/<name>/SKILL.md to flat skills/<name>/SKILL.md, resolving Q001. Zero name collisions across the former 15 domains (verified before moving — no renames needed). Domain grouping preserved only as a logical tag in this file's skill_domains array (each entry's path field now explicitly notes it is not a real filesystem path) and in each skill's own phase/tags frontmatter — not as a directory structure.
decisions.rationale: The domain-nested structure was confirmed empirically (Chunk 19 testing) to be undiscoverable by Claude Code — the exact same class of bug as the agents/<role>/AGENT.md issue (D013), just affecting ~10x more files. Fixed as its own dedicated PR per explicit direction, after Chunks 19 and 20 shipped, rather than blocking those on this larger, purely mechanical fix.
alternatives_rejected: Keep domain subdirectories and find a manifest-level override — researched during Q001's investigation, no working override found
Rename colliding skills to preserve some domain info in the name — unnecessary, zero collisions existed

decisions.decision: schemas/sdlc-config.schema.json and schemas/sdlc-manifest.schema.json (Draft 2020-12) formalize skills/sdlc-config-management and skills/artifact-manifest's already-documented Output Format shapes exactly, rather than inventing a new shape. sdlc-manifest.schema.json validates only the per-product manifest INSTANCE, not the master artifact-type catalog (which stays a prose table, extended over time — type is a free-form pattern, not a closed enum, to avoid needing a schema update on every new artifact-producing skill).
decisions.rationale: Both governance skills already had complete, worked JSON examples in their Output Format sections from when they were written (Chunk 18) — the schema's job was to encode what was already specified, not design something new. Tested against the real jsonschema library (Draft202012Validator): both skills' exact worked examples validate cleanly, and a battery of deliberately invalid instances (missing required fields, bad enums, malformed dates/semver/slugs, unknown fields, empty traceability refs) are all correctly rejected — 15 negative cases total across both schemas.
alternatives_rejected: Also schema-ize the type catalog as a closed enum — rejected per the skill's own statement that the catalog is a representative cross-section extended over time; a closed enum would need updating on every new artifact-producing skill

decisions.decision: Skill/agent smoke tests split into a Contract tier (a fast, cheap LLM-answered question about one documented fact — what the 6 broken *.fixture.sh files became once fixed) and a new Acceptance tier (a live agent dispatch that must actually invoke the named skill and produce the real work product — a written artifact or real code — validated structurally and, where a toolchain exists, mechanically). Contract stays the fast canary; Acceptance proves the agent can do its job, not just recite facts about it. Selection for --skill/--agent/--changed and the new automatic hook derives from agents' existing frontmatter skills: list (grepped for ownership) rather than a second, hand-maintained tag system.
decisions.rationale: The prior six skills/agents test files were pure two-variable shell fixtures that never sourced tests/lib/harness.sh — run-smoke-tests.sh's glob picked them up and silently reported 0 passed/0 failed, not a failure. Separately, even a fixed Q&A test ("what's the word limit?") never proves an agent can invoke a skill and produce its real output — Shafi's explicit objection. Reusing the skills: frontmatter block (already the single source of truth for which agent owns which skill) for selection avoids a second manifest that would drift from it; git diff --name-only drives change-based selection, the same idea as jest --onlyChanged / nx affected.
alternatives_rejected: A hand-maintained tag/manifest file mapping skills to owning agents and to test tiers — rejected: agents/*.md's skills: list already is that mapping; a second copy would just drift out of sync with it.

decisions.decision: Every live agent dispatch in tests/lib/harness.sh's smoke_test_acceptance (and tests/hooks/hooks-wiring.test.sh, fixed alongside) uses --permission-mode auto, not bypassPermissions or acceptEdits.
decisions.rationale: Found by live testing: --permission-mode bypassPermissions maps to --dangerously-skip-permissions, which Claude Code refuses to honor when the process runs as root (this environment does) — this was silently causing hooks-wiring.test.sh's second case to fail (the dispatch errored before attempting the write, so the file predictably never landed, and the test's first case — file absent after a blocked write — happened to read as a pass for the wrong reason). --permission-mode acceptEdits auto-accepts Write/Edit but still blocks Bash approval; several agents in this plugin declare tools: [Bash] only (backend-engineer, frontend-engineer — no Write tool at all, so they create files via Bash heredocs), and under acceptEdits those agents hang or error indefinitely waiting for a Bash approval that never arrives in a headless -p session. auto grants both non-interactively and was confirmed to still enforce this repo's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks correctly.
alternatives_rejected: bypassPermissions/--dangerously-skip-permissions — rejected: refused outright when running as root, which this environment does
acceptEdits — rejected: leaves Bash-only agents unable to create files non-interactively

decisions.decision: skills/ddd-agent-handoff replaces the originally proposed 'ddd-orchestrator' concept (a 14-role sub-agent network with its own references/assets/guidelines subtree and an embedded pytest test suite). Built instead as a single flat cross-cutting skill (phase: cross-cutting, owner: factory-governance, matching glossary-management/methodology-review) containing only an Agent Boundary Matrix (pointing to the 11 real agents and their existing skills) and a short Handoff Protocol. No new agents were created.
decisions.rationale: The 14 draft roles mapped onto this repo's existing 13 agents with zero true gaps once corrected — several draft rows were mislabeled (e.g. Context Map work belongs to domain-modeler, not enterprise-architect) or collapsed onto the same agent (DevOps+Platform -> platform-engineer; Security+Compliance -> security-architect/security-engineer). Separately, ~7 of the proposed reference files (ddd_glossary, ubiquitous_language, context_mapping_patterns, cqrs_event_sourcing, saga_patterns, event_storming_template, adr_template) duplicated content already owned by existing skills (aggregate-design, ubiquitous-language, context-map-patterns/bounded-context-mapping, cqrs-pattern, event-driven-patterns, event-storming-facilitation, adr-authoring) — recreating them would have created a second, competing source of truth for DDD terminology in a repo with a terminology-drift-detector hook. The draft's procedural 'Triage Algorithm' was also dropped as reasoning/decision-making that belongs in an Agent, not a Skill, per this repo's Component Architecture rule; the Agent Boundary Matrix (a selection-criteria table) was kept since CLAUDE.md explicitly allows that as Skill knowledge. Full analysis recorded on GitHub issue #48.
alternatives_rejected: Scaffold the meta-prompt literally (skill.md, pytest test suite, 14 fresh roles) — rejected: wrong filename/frontmatter shape for this repo's verified auto-discovery, and a test convention (embedded pytest) that contradicts CLAUDE.md's 'skills have no build step or test suite' rule
Keep the 14 conceptual roles as a separate taxonomy layered on top of the 13 agents — rejected: an unnecessary second vocabulary for the same 13 agents, adding indirection with no benefit
Build the full references/assets/guidelines package anyway alongside the 7 pre-existing overlapping skills — rejected: creates duplicate/competing DDD terminology

decisions.decision: Established the skill-refactor campaign's per-skill procedure using ddd-agent-handoff as the first case: one parent GitHub issue per skill, dependency-ordered sub-issues (one per references/assets file plus a final rewrite-SKILL.md step and a housekeeping step), and a mandatory gap-check against real industry practice (here: Team Topologies' three interaction modes, and Eric Evans' Domain-Driven Design directly) before finalizing the design. When the gap-check surfaces a genuinely missing skill (subdomain-distillation, for Evans Part IV Distillation) rather than misplaced content, pull it into the same plan as its own MVP-scoped sub-issue if a dependent file needs to reference it, instead of leaving it as an unscheduled idea.
decisions.rationale: Shafi's stated goal for this campaign is skills that are 'result-oriented for a proper software organization,' not prose — a mechanical progressive-disclosure split alone doesn't guarantee that; checking against a named, credible industry standard (here, the source text DDD itself is named after) is what caught two real gaps (Core/Supporting/Generic Subdomain classification as the primary mode-selection input; the operational-pause vs. breakthrough-triggered-refactor distinction for resumed sessions) that a generic 'add more detail' pass would likely have missed. Pulling subdomain-distillation in as an MVP sub-issue (rather than deferring it) avoided handoff-protocol.md shipping with a pointer to a skill that didn't exist yet.
alternatives_rejected: Defer subdomain-distillation as a queued idea for its own future session — rejected once handoff-protocol.md's Mode Selection Criteria was designed to depend on it; a real dependency should not ship broken

Skip the Evans gap-check and treat the Team-Topologies-anchored design as sufficient — rejected: Shafi explicitly asked to check against the source text before treating the plan as done, and it surfaced two real gaps, not just polish

decisions.decision: Standardize on Miro for visual/board-style artifacts across skills and agents, but as structured board specs only for now (a new miro-board-notation skill defining Miro's real element vocabulary — sticky note, shape, frame, connector, text — and a two-table spec format), not a live API/MCP integration. The same MVP-dependency-pull pattern from D021 applied again: miro-board-notation was pulled into the subdomain-distillation refactor plan as its own sub-issue (#69) because 3 dependent files (a Wardley Map, a Domain Vision Board, and the classification canvas) needed it to exist.
decisions.rationale: Checked via claude mcp list before writing any Miro-related content: no Miro MCP/API connection exists in this environment, and this repo's mcp/ directory is an explicitly deferred placeholder per CLAUDE.md. Writing diagrams as Miro-vocabulary board specs now costs nothing extra (they're still buildable by hand or readable as structured tables) and means zero rework once a real Miro connection exists later — the alternative (plain prose diagrams now, retrofit to Miro's vocabulary later) would require rewriting every visual artifact this campaign produces in the meantime.
alternatives_rejected: Wire up a live Miro MCP/API connection now — rejected per Shafi's explicit choice; no account/token readiness signal was given, and premature integration risks building against the wrong API shape before more skills actually need to render boards

Keep diagrams as plain prose/tables with no Miro-specific vocabulary — rejected: defeats the stated goal of standardizing on Miro, and would require retrofitting every visual artifact produced during this campaign later

decisions.decision: Adopt micro-frontend architecture for this plugin's frontend (shell + independently-deployable remotes, one per Bounded-Context-aligned fragment, composed via Module Federation over Vite) as a deliberate decision, not an inferred default. Triggered by a question about where CSS/styling strategy should live; escalated into a full architecture pivot once Shafi confirmed the organizational precondition every source book gates adoption on (multiple teams needing independent release cadence) — Shafi stated this repo anticipates multiple future products and teams contributing.
decisions.rationale: The research this campaign already produced (research/micro-frontends/, 4 books) concluded a solo-operator, single-product context does NOT meet the bar for micro-frontends per every book's own decision framework -- Claude flagged this tension explicitly before proceeding rather than silently building content contradicting the repo's own prior research. Shafi's clarification (multiple future products/teams) resolved it: team count, not codebase size, is the actual trigger per Mezzalira, and that precondition is now real for this repo's stated future, even though only one frontend-engineer agent builds every fragment today.
alternatives_rejected: Proceed without flagging the tension against the existing research -- rejected: would have built skill content contradicting conclusions already on record in the same repo, undermining the research's credibility

Defer the architecture decision until multiple teams actually exist -- rejected per Shafi's explicit instruction to adopt it from the beginning, anticipating the future need rather than retrofitting later

decisions.decision: End the plan-start/plan-exit GitHub Project ceremony (parent issue + numbered sub-issues via save_draft/plan_exit) for future individual skill refactors. Skill refactors continue directly -- read the current skill, gap-check against research/industry sources, design a progressive-disclosure split, rewrite, commit -- without a new parent issue + sub-issue set per skill. Already-open sub-issues from in-flight plans (this chunk's #90-#98) were still completed via the existing exec-start/exec-complete flow rather than abandoned mid-flight, since abandoning already-created GitHub tracking would leave orphaned issues.
decisions.rationale: Shafi's explicit instruction, given after two full campaign cycles (ddd-agent-handoff issue #54, subdomain-distillation issue #68) and mid-way through a third (this chunk, issue #89): the plan/execute ceremony's value was establishing a repeatable, well-understood procedure (per D021's per-skill process) -- once demonstrated and understood, repeating the ceremony for every additional skill adds overhead without adding safety, given the process itself (gap-check against real sources, progressive disclosure, verification) is what's load-bearing, not the GitHub issue tracking around it.
alternatives_rejected: Keep using plan-start/plan-exit for every future skill -- rejected per Shafi's explicit instruction once momentum and shared understanding were established

Also abandon the already-open #90-#98 sub-issues' tracking retroactively -- rejected: they were already created and tracked; finishing them via the existing lightweight exec-start/exec-complete flow avoided orphaning GitHub state for no benefit

decisions.decision: Re-introduced GitHub issue/sub-issue tracking (reversing D024's default, for this case) using a new pattern: an issue-level integration branch with its own draft PR, sub-issue branches cut from and PRs targeting that integration branch (not main) via exec_start.py's new --base flag, merged into the integration branch by Claude in sequence as each sub-issue completes, with only the single integration-branch-to-main PR left for Shafi to review and merge. Used for the acceptance-sign-off refactor (issue #110, sub-issues #112-#115, integration PR #111).
decisions.rationale: Shafi explicitly requested 'detailed issues and sub-issues and relevant PRs' for this refactor and asked that it be 'done automatically,' with only one final PR requiring his review -- a different, heavier-weight shape than D024's default direct-commit process, requested for this specific case rather than a reversal of D024 generally. The issue-level-branch pattern satisfies both asks at once: full GitHub tracking/traceability per sub-issue, but a single review/merge point for Shafi rather than one per sub-issue.
alternatives_rejected: Merge every sub-issue PR directly into main as in the original D021-era process -- rejected: contradicts 'I will review and merge the final PR,' which implies exactly one PR for Shafi to handle, not one per sub-issue

Skip GitHub issues entirely per D024's default -- rejected: contradicts this specific request for 'detailed issues and sub-issues,' which D024 did not forbid for cases where Shafi explicitly asks for it again

decisions.decision: For issue-level-integration-branch plans (D025 pattern), do not call plan_status.py done when sub-issue work finishes merging into the integration branch -- only after Shafi has actually merged the final integration-branch-to-main PR. The parent GitHub issue itself still auto-closes correctly via its 'Closes #N' body text at that real merge; this decision only concerns the Project board's Status field, which plan_status.py done updates.
decisions.rationale: Direct correction from Shafi for issue #120: 'the parent issue should not be closed until the main PR is merged by me.' Investigation showed issue #110's actual GitHub close had in fact fired at the correct time (Shafi's real merge of PR #111) -- the real mistake was calling plan_status.py done immediately once sub-issues landed on the integration branch, before that merge, which prematurely marked the Project board Status as Done while the final PR was still awaiting Shafi's review.
alternatives_rejected: Leave the timing as-is on the theory that the GitHub issue-close mechanism is what actually matters -- rejected: Shafi's feedback was about the signal the Project board Status field sends, not just the issue-close event, and a premature Done status is still a misleading signal even if the issue itself closes correctly later

decisions.decision: Introduce Architecture Principle as a new, distinct output artifact type (a per-product PRINCIPLES.md catalog, owned by enterprise-architect via adr-authoring) alongside the existing ADR artifact type -- durable, cross-cutting guidance that many future ADRs cite, as opposed to a single point-in-time decision. Scoped narrowly: taught inside adr-authoring's own references/architecture-principles.md (format template, generalization test, storage convention, one illustrative worked example), not spun off into a separate skill file.
decisions.rationale: Fundamentals of Software Architecture Ch. 18 (research/software-architecture/fundamentals-of-software-architecture-richards-ford.md) was the only research source that named adr-authoring as a primary refactor target, and its one genuine gap was exactly this missing distinction -- several ADR-worthy items already in this repo (e.g., integration-design's 'asynchronous is the default' prose rule) are really principles, not decisions, and adr-authoring had no separate authoring path for them, risking durable guidance getting buried and silently lost inside a single ADR's Rationale if that ADR is ever superseded. Kept inside adr-authoring rather than a new skill because the artifact is small (one companion format + template) and no other skill or agent currently needs to reference Principle-authoring mechanics independently of ADR-authoring -- the MVP-dependency-pull threshold from D021 (pull in a new skill only when a real dependent need exists) was not met.
alternatives_rejected: Spin off a separate architecture-principle-authoring skill -- rejected: no dependent skill/agent needs Principle mechanics independently of adr-authoring today; would add a discovery/maintenance surface for a companion concept this small

Retroactively formalize this repo's own existing conventions (CLAUDE.md's tables, integration-design's prose rule) as named Principle records now -- rejected as out of scope for a single-skill content refactor; recorded as open question Q003 for Shafi to decide separately

Leave the decision-vs-principle distinction as prose-only guidance inside adr-authoring's Rationale section with no dedicated artifact type -- rejected: the book's own gap analysis is specifically that this needs a distinct, citable artifact, not just advice to write better ADRs

decisions.decision: Adopt a formalized scripts/ and assets/ subdirectory convention for individual skills (skills/<name>/scripts/*.sh, skills/<name>/assets/*), alongside the existing references/ progressive-disclosure tier -- codified in a new cross-cutting skill, skill-authoring-standards, and a short new CLAUDE.md section. A skill-owned script is invoked by the agent applying that skill (via the Bash tool, at a path the skill's own body names), distinct from the pre-existing repo-root scripts/ convention (hook- or command-invoked) -- same Scripts = Actions rule, different invocation context. adr-authoring (rebuilt v3.0.0) is the first real skill to use this shape: assets/adr-template.md (copyable) plus scripts/scaffold-adr.sh and scripts/validate-adr.sh (deterministic generation/validation), each with its own tests/scripts/*.test.sh.
decisions.rationale: research/ai-agent-engineering/mastering-claude-code-agent-skills-gale.md established the three-tier progressive disclosure rubric (metadata/body/references) already correctly practiced by several skills, but found no repo precedent for scripts/assets since this repo had never used them -- Shafi explicitly asked for skills to move beyond prose-only templates into scripts that actually generate and validate artifacts (documents, code, test suites, reviews), matching the real Claude Agent Skills format's scripts/+assets/ convention rather than this repo's own invented shape. Scoped to skill-authoring-standards (not a new component type in CLAUDE.md's closed Component Architecture table) because scripts/assets are sub-parts of the existing Skill component, not a new top-level component -- the existing Scripts = Actions rule already governs the behavior, only the location and caller differ.
alternatives_rejected: Leave scripts/assets undocumented and let each skill invent its own ad hoc convention as the need arises -- rejected: exactly the 'imitate whichever skill was refactored most recently' problem skill-authoring-standards exists to end, and the whole point of doing this now is to establish one citable convention before more skills adopt it inconsistently

Treat skill-owned scripts as a new top-level component type distinct from the existing repo-root Scripts -- rejected: the underlying rule (atomic, deterministic, stateless, single-purpose) is identical; only the invocation context differs, which does not warrant a new row in CLAUDE.md's Component Architecture table

Retrofit scripts/assets onto the other ~140 existing skills as part of this same chunk -- rejected: applying the new standard happens going forward, per refactor session, not as a retrofit-everything chunk, matching this repo's established forward-apply pattern for other skill-shape changes

decisions.decision: Establish research/domain-driven-design/ as a new research cluster (Evans' Domain-Driven Design, Vernon's Implementing Domain-Driven Design / Effective Aggregate Design, Khononov's Learning Domain-Driven Design), researched as a prerequisite phase before extensively rebuilding skills/aggregate-design/SKILL.md, rather than writing the rebuild from general LLM knowledge of these widely-known books. Corrected aggregate-design's prior header framing ('these rules are non-negotiable') to match Vernon's own explicitly-not-absolutist stance, with a documented, criteria-gated exception process replacing false absolutism.
decisions.rationale: Shafi asked for an extensive rebuild of aggregate-design including 'every possible information, practice, decision, nuance' from the DDD Aggregate literature, split across multiple references/ files with explicit decision-tree structure. Checking research/ first (per this repo's own established discipline) found no dedicated research existed for the actual foundational DDD Aggregate texts, despite aggregate-design's existing five rules clearly summarizing them -- writing exhaustive content without first researching the primary sources would be exactly the 'memory-sourced content' anti-pattern requirements-analysis already names as a defect. Vernon's research (research/domain-driven-design/implementing-ddd-vernon.md) surfaced the non-negotiable-vs-Vernon's-real-position gap as the single most consequential finding of the whole rebuild -- a repo-authored skill had drifted to a stricter position than its own primary source actually holds.
alternatives_rejected: Write the rebuild directly from general knowledge of Evans/Vernon/Khononov without a dedicated research pass, given how widely known these books are -- rejected: this is precisely the 'memory-sourced' risk this repo's own requirements-analysis skill names as a defect, and the non-negotiable-vs-Vernon's-real-position finding would likely have been missed without the dedicated, grounded research pass that specifically re-examined the existing skill's claims against the source

Keep the DDD research folded into the existing software-architecture cluster rather than a new dedicated cluster -- rejected: DDD tactical/strategic design is a distinct discipline from general software architecture, and a dedicated cluster keeps the three foundational DDD texts discoverable together for whichever skill needs them next (bounded-context-mapping, subdomain-distillation, domain-event-catalog all cite DDD literature and could benefit from the same cluster later)

Merge Khononov's Business Logic Design Pattern gate and Event Sourcing content into the originally-planned reference file structure rather than absorbing them into existing files (d7's go-implementation-patterns.md, d8's decision-trees-and-worksheets.md) -- rejected as unnecessary: both additions fit naturally into already-planned files without requiring new sub-issues or GitHub issue renumbering after issues were already created

decisions.decision: Reorganize alerting-rules-design's top-level framing around Google's Four Golden Signals (Latency, Traffic, Errors, Saturation) and add a generic, resource-agnostic Saturation alert pattern, rather than leaving Saturation implicit or pipeline-specific-only. Correct the burn-rate table's citation to name two distinct sources precisely: the 2016 SRE book for the error-budget/burn-rate concept, the 2018 SRE Workbook for the specific 14.4x/6x/1x multiplier table -- never crediting one book with the other's content.
decisions.rationale: research/devops-and-delivery/site-reliability-engineering-beyer-jones-petoff-murphy.md found the skill's existing content was correct but under-attributed: the burn-rate table's exact numbers are a 2018 SRE Workbook artifact this 2016 book only conceptually enables, and Latency/Traffic/Errors were implicitly present via SLO burn while Saturation had no generic treatment at all -- only pipeline-specific DLQ/lag indicators existed, which are freshness-specific, not a reusable pattern. Fixing attribution and adding the missing fourth signal turns received constants into auditable, correctly-sourced content without changing anything that was already correct.
alternatives_rejected: Leave the burn-rate table citation as-is (uncited) since the numbers themselves are correct and citation is a documentation-quality concern, not a correctness bug -- rejected: CLAUDE.md's artifact standards require traceability, and an uncited received constant cannot be recomputed if the SLO window ever changes, which is a real, not merely cosmetic, gap

Build a full generic saturation-alerting skill or expand prometheus-metrics-design instead of adding the pattern inside alerting-rules-design -- rejected: prometheus-metrics-design already computes the saturation ratio as a dashboard query; the gap is specifically that no alert reads it, which is alerting-rules-design's domain, not a new metrics-design concern

Build a standalone postmortem-authoring skill now, since two independent research sources (this book and the DevOps Handbook) both flagged it as a real gap -- rejected as out of scope for this issue; noted as a follow-up candidate in the parent issue's body rather than built here, keeping this rebuild's scope to alerting-rules-design's own domain

decisions.decision: Cite analytics-requirements' vanity-metric checklist as Croll & Yoskovitz's actionable-vs-vanity-metric framework (Lean Analytics, 2013) and add a clarifying distinction between the book's One Metric That Matters (OMTM -- stage-relative, deliberately rotating as the business's single biggest risk changes) and this repo's North Star Metric (okr-authoring -- fixed for the duration of an OKR cycle). Do not add OMTM as a new canonical glossary term at this time.
decisions.rationale: research/data-and-analytics/lean-analytics-croll-yoskovitz.md found the skill's existing five-point checklist independently reinvents most of the book's own framework without citing it, and separately found that OMTM and North Star Metric are superficially similar but genuinely distinct on one load-bearing dimension (durability vs. disposability) -- a reader who assumed they were the same term under different names would be wrong in a way that matters for how a requirement's priority argument should be read. The research file itself explicitly cautioned that adding OMTM to the canonical glossary is premature on the strength of one skill's cross-reference alone, since this repo has not adopted stage-based rotating focus as a standing practice -- that caution was followed rather than overridden.
alternatives_rejected: Add OMTM to the canonical glossary now, on the theory that any term explained in a skill body should also be glossaried -- rejected per the research file's own explicit caution: a term mentioned once for clarification purposes is not the same as a term this repo's artifacts actually use as a working concept, and premature glossary entries dilute the glossary's signal

Treat OMTM and North Star Metric as interchangeable and merge the concepts rather than distinguishing them -- rejected: the two differ on a dimension (fixed-per-cycle vs. deliberately rotating) that changes how a requirement's priority argument should be read, so merging them would silently discard real information the research surfaced

Propose a Lean Analytics stage-framework (Empathy/Stickiness/Virality/Revenue/Scale) skill or practice, since the book's OMTM concept is normally paired with it -- rejected as a poor fit for this repo's single, non-viral B2B product, per the research file's own Candidate New Skills/Agents section

decisions.decision: Extend api-contract-design with four patterns from JJ Geewax's API Design Patterns: a named custom-method escape hatch (POST /{resource}:verb) alongside the existing 'Verb endpoints' anti-pattern; a fully-specified Operation resource shape for the 202 Accepted status-check response, reusing the skill's existing ErrorResponse.error object by reference rather than redefining a new error type; a resource-revisions (etag/If-Match) optimistic-concurrency mechanism distinct from the existing 409 Conflict business-rule row; and a field-mask convention clarifying PATCH partial-update semantics. Explicitly declined to change the skill's existing per-field-query-parameter filtering convention to match the book's filter-expression-string approach.
decisions.rationale: research/software-architecture/api-design-patterns-geewax.md found api-contract-design had zero primary-source grounding despite being the authoritative contract between backend-engineer and frontend-engineer, and identified four specific, narrow gaps where the skill's existing conventions left a real question unanswered (most consequentially, what a 202 Accepted status URL actually returns when polled) rather than broad disagreement with anything already built. Declined the filtering-convention change because implementing a filter-expression grammar is real engineering cost CLAUDE.md's Budget and Frugality principle would weigh against without a concrete need for compound/boolean filter logic -- the research file itself frames the skill's existing named-parameter approach as a deliberate, defensible choice, not an oversight to fix.
alternatives_rejected: Migrate the skill's filtering convention to Geewax's single filter-expression-string parameter to match the book more closely -- rejected: this is real, unjustified implementation cost against a frugal, single-operator context with no concrete need for compound filter logic yet; the research file itself argues against this change

Treat this as a modest, single-file content addition like the analytics-requirements precedent rather than a genuine multi-file rebuild -- rejected: the skill was already 323 lines before any additions, past the split threshold on its own, and the four new patterns (each with worked YAML examples) add substantial, cohesive new content that reads far better as a dedicated references/ file than crammed into an already-long single file

Adopt Geewax's full Google-AIP-style API design system (gRPC/Protocol-Buffers-oriented conventions, the complete google.rpc.Status error model) wholesale -- rejected: most of that ground is irrelevant to this repo's REST/OpenAPI-only stack; only the REST-applicable subset (custom methods, LRO shape, revisions, field masks) closes an actual gap

decisions.decision: Adopt six canonical labels (discovery, agent, skill, bug, documentation, enhancement -- multiple allowed per item) as mandatory on every issue, sub-issue, and PR in the SKILL GEN Project. Retroactively labeled all 249 existing issues/PRs by title-pattern classification, spot-checked and verified 249/249 correct. Enforced going forward by requiring --labels on plan_start.py and save_draft.py add (validated before any GitHub mutation runs), with exec_start.py mirroring a sub-issue's labels onto its PR rather than asking for a separate choice. Commits are explicitly out of scope -- GitHub has no commit-label mechanism, and Shafi confirmed conventional-commit prefixes are not wanted either.
decisions.rationale: Shafi asked for consistent, retroactive-and-future labeling across the project's issues/sub-issues/PRs/commits. Applying the fix uncovered a second GraphQL 'Projects (classic)' deprecation bug beyond the one skill-refactor.md already warns about for gh issue edit body edits: gh pr edit --add-label fails outright on this repo (exit 1, label never applied) via the same deprecated-field GraphQL path, while gh issue edit --add-label works. Standardized both the retroactive script and the new project.py/gh.py tooling on the REST labels endpoint (gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n>/labels, which treats PRs as issues) instead, since it is confirmed reliable for both and removes the split-path inconsistency entirely.
alternatives_rejected: Use gh pr edit --add-label for PR labeling as originally implemented -- rejected after empirical failure: it returns exit 1 and never applies the label on this repo, the same category of GraphQL Projects-classic bug skill-refactor.md already documents for gh issue edit body edits

Let exec_start.py pass --label flags directly on gh pr create -- rejected as an unverified assumption riding on the same buggy code path; replaced with applying labels via the proven-reliable REST endpoint immediately after PR creation, using the sub-issue's already-set labels as the single source of truth

Treat commits as in-scope via conventional-commit-style prefixes (feat:/fix:/etc.) -- rejected per Shafi's explicit answer: commits are skipped entirely rather than inventing a parallel, unrequested convention

decisions.decision: Rebuild artifact-manifest (Chunk 41, issue #251) as an evidence-based restructuring of its own existing content -- thin SKILL.md + references/artifact-type-catalog.md + references/manifest-worked-example.md + assets/manifest-instance-template.json -- rather than a content addition grounded in new book research, since Wave 1 discovery (sub-issue #252) confirmed no book in the 50-book research/ corpus is squarely about software/documentation artifact registries or traceability matrices. Declined a skill-owned scaffold/validate script for this skill: schemas/sdlc-manifest.schema.json and tests/schemas/sdlc-manifest.test.py already formalize and test the per-product instance shape, so a script would duplicate existing coverage rather than fill a gap.
decisions.rationale: Every prior skill-refactor effort's Wave 1 discovery either found a genuinely new book to research or confirmed an existing book's coverage already applied to the target skill. This is the first case where discovery confirmed neither -- the skill's actual subject matter (a plugin-internal artifact registry) sits outside every researched cluster's scope, including the data-governance-and-mdm cluster's closest tangential content (DAMA-DMBOK Ch. 12 Metadata Management, Loshin's MDM ID/lifecycle concepts), which are both scoped to governing data assets, not SDLC/documentation artifacts. Proceeding without forcing a false-positive research grounding, and instead restructuring the skill's own already-sound content into the shape sibling governance skills (ddd-agent-handoff, glossary-management, methodology-review) already settled on, keeps the skill-authoring-standards rebuild honest about what discovery actually found, per the standing 'calibrated honesty' norm (see the research-books-inventory memory's note on the 16-book batch's low-candidate-count books).
alternatives_rejected: Force-fit DAMA-DMBOK's Metadata Management chapter as grounding content for artifact-manifest, since it is the closest thematic match in the corpus -- rejected: that chapter's own Applies To table already scopes its findings to data-asset-governance skills (data-classification, canonical-data-model, etc.), not to this skill, and citing it here would misattribute content the skill's rebuild did not actually derive from it

Skip the rebuild entirely since no new research grounds it -- rejected: the skill was still a flat 195-line file past the point where sibling governance skills already adopted progressive disclosure, and the skill-authoring-standards shape rubric applies independent of whether a specific rebuild happens to be research-driven

Add a skill-owned scaffold/validate script pair to match every prior rebuilt skill's pattern -- rejected as scope creep: this skill's output is validated by an existing JSON Schema (schemas/sdlc-manifest.schema.json) and existing test (tests/schemas/sdlc-manifest.test.py) already, so a redundant script would duplicate coverage rather than close a real gap

decisions.decision: Rebuild bdd-feature-file (Chunk 42, issue #266) as a modest content addition -- one new references/ file, one scaffold/validate script pair, one asset template -- grounded in new research/testing/specification-by-example-adzic.md (Gojko Adzic) plus consolidation of four already-existing tangential research files. Added the Three Amigos naming (Crispin & Gregory's finding, sharpened by Adzic's checkable Specification Workshop definition-of-ready), the missing half of Living Documentation's actual definition (Adzic's most consequential finding for this skill), the Key Examples minimality principle, and one Anti-Patterns row for untended specification growth. decisions.rationale: Wave 1 discovery's #268 sub-issue confirmed the skill already fully implements Ken Pugh's ATDD declarative-vs-imperative point (a provenance note, not new content) and that Cohn/Lee/Jorgensen's research has no direct finding for this skill. The #267 sub-issue's new Adzic research found the skill's existing Living Documentation section was a faithful but partial implementation of Adzic's own, more precise definition -- the section already captured 'current because tested in CI' but never named the second half (mechanically deriving a browsable documentation artifact from the executed suite), which is the actual payoff Adzic's practice is named for. This is the second skill-refactor effort (after artifact-manifest, D034) where Wave 1's two discovery sub-issues split cleanly into 'confirm existing coverage' and 'new book research' running in the same wave, rather than one sub-issue serving both jobs -- appropriate here because a genuine, well-justified new-book target existed (an already-used-but-uncredited glossary term) alongside real existing tangential coverage worth consolidating first.
alternatives_rejected: Treat the Three Amigos naming gap alone as sufficient grounds for the rebuild, skipping new Adzic research -- rejected: 'Specification by Example' was already a load-bearing, cited glossary term with no source book ever researched, and BDD is a non-negotiable CLAUDE.md methodology with (until this chunk) zero primary-source grounding for the skill that implements it -- the same category of gap api-contract-design's rebuild (D032) closed for its own domain

Fold the Key Examples minimality principle into the existing Golden Triangle section as a rule change rather than a complementary addition -- rejected: the two operate on different axes (breadth-of-angles vs economy-of-examples-per-angle) per the research file's own explicit finding; conflating them would misrepresent Adzic's actual, narrower claim

Skip the scaffold/validate script pair since the content findings were modest -- rejected: unlike artifact-manifest (where an existing JSON Schema and test already covered validation), bdd-feature-file's .feature output had no existing mechanical check anywhere, and the Golden-Triangle-tag/imperative-leakage/multi-When checks are all genuinely new, checkable ground worth automating

decisions.decision: Rebuild beta-program-design (Chunk 43, issue #282) as a modest content addition -- one new references/ file, one scaffold/validate script pair, one asset template -- grounded in new research/product-strategy-and-gtm/four-steps-to-the-epiphany-blank.md (Steve Blank's Customer Development methodology) plus consolidation of three already-existing tangential research files. Added two new Participant Selection criteria (credible reference for stage-expansion, per Moore; evidence of prior self-funded effort, per Blank's earlyvangelist condition 2), a third Graduation Criteria outcome (pivot, alongside extend/remediate), and an explicit outside-the-building check before a qualitative graduation bar is marked met. Added 5 new canonical glossary terms (Customer Development, Customer Validation, Earlyvangelist, Get Out of the Building, Pivot), including a bidirectional disambiguation between the new Customer Validation entry and the existing Product Validation entry, since Blank's research file explicitly flagged the two as a near-duplicate collision risk if added carelessly.
decisions.rationale: Wave 1 discovery's #284 sub-issue confirmed the skill already correctly delegates anti-leading-question discipline to feedback-template (a non-gap) and surfaced one real, modest gap from Moore's Crossing the Chasm (the credible-reference criterion) that the book's own Applies To table had never checked against this specific skill. The #283 sub-issue's new Blank research found the single most consequential fact this repo's skill-refactor campaign has surfaced to date: CLAUDE.md's own 'Customer Validation' phase name -- used across the entire eight-phase model, not just this one skill -- is literally Steve Blank's Customer Development terminology, never once researched despite being load-bearing repo-wide. The research confirmed this skill's four internal stages map cleanly as a subdivision within Blank's single Customer Validation stage (not a conflation of multiple Blank stages), which is a validating finding, not a defect -- but it also surfaced three genuine, additive content gaps (a second Participant Selection criterion distinct from Moore's, the pivot outcome, and the outside-the-building check) that no prior discovery pass had found because no prior pass had researched Blank's methodology at all.
alternatives_rejected: Treat this as purely a provenance/naming exercise (confirm the phase name traces to Blank, add glossary terms, stop there) since the stage-mapping check came back clean -- rejected: Blank's earlyvangelist and pivot concepts are genuinely separate, checkable content beyond the naming confirmation, and the research file's own Actionable Techniques section gives concrete, adoptable techniques (the self-funded-effort screening question, the segment/problem/solution/process diagnostic) that would be a real loss to leave uncaptured just because the headline finding was a confirmation rather than a correction

Merge the new 'credible reference' and 'prior self-funded effort' Participant Selection criteria into one combined row since both come from early-customer-screening research -- rejected per the Blank research file's own explicit reasoning: the two predict different things (self-funded effort predicts whether feedback reflects real motivated pain; credible reference predicts whether the resulting endorsement transfers to open beta), so collapsing them would lose a real distinction the research surfaced

Leave the Customer Validation and Product Validation glossary entries as originally drafted without adding a cross-reference in Product Validation's own text -- rejected: a one-directional disambiguation (only the new entry pointing at the old one) would let a reader who looks up Product Validation first miss the distinction entirely; both entries now cross-reference each other

Housekeeping for the full campaign collected in issue #407 (this entry): CLAUDE.md /init improvements (layout section additions, skill-refactor branch-naming pattern, contract-test requirement), 3 new canonical glossary terms (ARIA, Core Web Vitals, WCAG) added in a new Frontend Engineering section, CHANGELOG entries for all 13 individual rebuilds, and sdlc-context.json updated with this decision.
decisions.rationale: The grouped campaign (Chunk 44, D037) established the right research-before-writing discipline and fixed two real bugs in react-graph-visualization, but the group-level sub-issues meant that each skill's body was checked once in context with 2-4 sibling skills rather than as a standalone review. The individual rebuild pass gave each skill its own focused session: cross-references were verified against actual current content on the branch rather than assumed states, SKILL.md bodies were tightened to the ~200-line progressive-disclosure threshold, and every skill that had no contract test gained one. The per-skill-sub-issue pattern (D025) had already been validated across access-control-model (#120), adr-authoring (#128), acceptance-criteria (#145), acceptance-sign-off (#155), access-control-model (#165), aggregate-design (#175), alerting-rules-design (#199), analytics-requirements (#217), api-contract-design (#231), artifact-manifest (#251), bdd-feature-file (#266), and beta-program-design (#282) — all of them individual skills with their own issue, not part of a grouped pass. Applying the same pattern to the react-* domain was consistent with established practice.
alternatives_rejected: Run a second grouped campaign (4 skills per sub-issue) rather than individual per-skill issues — rejected: the individual-skill pattern already has its own exec_start.py / exec_complete.py tooling and yields a focused, fully-auditable commit per skill; a second grouped pass would have the same coverage-per-sub-issue limitation the first pass had

Treat the cross-cutting group's zero-change result as final and skip individual rebuilds for react-accessibility, react-observability, react-performance-optimization, and react-dockerfile — rejected: a 'nothing applies' result from a group-level sub-issue with 4 skills in context means the research was correct in aggregate, not necessarily that each skill's own body is already at the progressive-disclosure depth standard — the individual rebuilds confirmed that all four needed reference splits and contract tests

Grouping by related skill cluster preserves full discovery-before-implementation rigor and per-skill verification while keeping the campaign's GitHub footprint tractable -- a scale adaptation to the mechanics of an already-proven process, not a departure from its discipline.
alternatives_rejected: Run 24 fully independent single-skill campaigns -- rejected: infeasible at the time budget implied and would produce ~170 sub-issues/PRs for the Go domain alone

Skip GitHub tracking entirely reverting to D024's no-ceremony default -- rejected: Shafi invoked /skill-refactor specifically, and the two-wave GitHub-tracked process is this repo's active convention for every skill rebuild

Run the Go and React domain campaigns concurrently on separate branches -- rejected after empirically hitting the constraint: the local ghp tooling only supports one active plan at a time via local state.json
Manufacture equally-deep content for every group regardless of what research actually found -- rejected: two groups had no direct research finding and were reported honestly as shape-only work

This repo's acceptance-criteria + bdd-feature-file + example-mapping pairing already is an ATDD practice in substance (examples-first collaborative derivation, now correctly sequenced per decision in Chunk 28), and research/requirements-and-user-stories/lean-agile-atdd-pugh.md noted ATDD's absence from the methodology table is inconsistent with TDD/BDD both being listed there. Concrete candidates: integration-design's 'asynchronous is the default for cross-Bounded-Context communication' prose rule, and several items in CLAUDE.md's own Non-Negotiable Methodology / Tech Stack Defaults tables that function as principles but are never named as such. anti_patterns: Skill that reasons or decides — reasoning belongs in an Agent
Agent that stores large domain knowledge — knowledge belongs in Skills
Command that contains methodology or domain expertise — belongs in Skills
Hook that runs a workflow — hooks validate only, they do not orchestrate
Script that makes business decisions — decisions belong in Agents
MCP that implements business workflows — MCPs expose atomic capabilities only
Agent with overlapping responsibilities — every agent has single, non-overlapping ownership
